answerNotes.PEACH: A peach has a fuzzy skin and a hard pit. A nectarine is a close relative with smooth skin.
answerNotes.PIE: A pie has a filling supported or enclosed by pastry. Not every pie has a top crust.
answerNotes.CRUST: Crust can mean a pie's pastry shell or a loaf's baked outer surface. Both are outer parts, but they are made differently.
answerNotes.FRUIT: Everyday fruit dishes can mix several kinds of plant produce. The serving word is culinary and does not require a botanical classification.
answerNotes.JUICE: Juice is liquid released from fruit or vegetables. Pulp is the soft plant material that may remain mixed into it.
answerNotes.SLICE: A slice is a flat cut portion of food. Slice can also be the action of cutting food into those portions.
answerNotes.PAN: Pan is a broad kitchen word. A frying pan is used on a stove, while a loaf pan holds dough or batter in the oven.
answerNotes.OVEN: An oven cooks with heat surrounding the food. That differs from the direct bottom heat under a pan on a stovetop.
answerNotes.BAKE: Baking uses dry heat in an oven. Boiling instead cooks food in bubbling liquid.
answerNotes.FLOUR: Flour is ground grain used in baking. The fine powder is different from whole kernels even when both come from the same crop.
answerNotes.SUGAR: Sugar sweetens baking mixtures and drinks. Granulated sugar and powdered sugar have different textures despite sharing the same sweet ingredient.
